title: Financial Accounting I
topics: Final accounts of a sole trader
Source documents and books of original entry

items.q: A machine costing 240000 naira has an expected value of 60000 naira at the end of its life of 4 years. What is the yearly charge using the straight line method?
items.s: Yearly charge = (cost - end value)/life = (240000 - 60000)/4 = 45000 naira.

items.q: A trader has receivables of 720000 naira. A customer who owes 38000 naira is declared unable to pay and the amount is written off. What figure for receivables remains?
items.s: Remaining receivables = 720000 - 38000 = 682000 naira.

items.q: Goods with a list price of 480000 naira are sold subject to a trade discount of 5 percent. What is the amount charged to the customer?
items.s: Amount charged = list price x (100 - discount)/100 = 480000 x (100 - 5)/100 = 456000 naira.

items.q: Opening stock was 95000 naira, purchases were 240000 naira and closing stock was 105000 naira. What is the cost of the goods sold?
items.s: Cost of goods sold = opening stock + purchases - closing stock = 95000 + 240000 - 105000 = 230000 naira.
items.t: Final accounts of a sole trader

items.q: Sales for the year were 620000 naira and the cost of the goods sold was 410000 naira. What is the gross profit?
items.s: Gross profit = sales - cost of goods sold = 620000 - 410000 = 210000 naira.
items.t: Final accounts of a sole trader

items.q: Goods costing 180000 naira are to be sold at a mark-up of 20 percent on cost. What is the selling price?
items.s: Selling price = cost x (100 + mark-up)/100 = 180000 x (100 + 20)/100 = 216000 naira.
items.t: Final accounts of a sole trader

items.q: A petty cash float of 25000 naira is reimbursed at the end of the month when 4650 naira is left in the box. How much is paid back into the float?
items.s: Reimbursement = float - cash left = 25000 - 4650 = 20350 naira.
items.t: Source documents and books of original entry

items.q: The debit column of a trial balance totals 320000 naira and the credit column totals 307000 naira. What amount is carried to the suspense account?
items.s: Suspense = difference between the two columns = 320000 - 307000 = 13000 naira.

items.q: Equipment costing 300000 naira is expected to be worth 50000 naira after 8 years and is written off evenly. What is the total charged against profit after 3 years?
items.s: Total charge = years x (cost - end value)/life = 3 x (300000 - 50000)/8 = 93750 naira.

items.q: A vehicle costing 750000 naira has a scrap value of 80000 naira and a life of 10 years and is written off evenly. What amount is carried in the books after 4 years?
items.s: Amount carried = cost - years x (cost - scrap)/life = 750000 - 4 x (750000 - 80000)/10 = 482000 naira.

items.q: An asset is bought for 350000 naira and is written down at 15 percent each year on the reducing balance. What is the charge for the first year?
items.s: First year charge = cost x rate = 350000 x 15/100 = 52500 naira.

items.q: A plant costing 625000 naira is written down at 20 percent each year on the reducing balance. What amount is carried in the books at the end of 2 years?
items.s: Amount carried = cost x (1 - rate/100)^years = 625000 x (1 - 20/100)^2 = 400000 naira.

items.q: An asset bought for 720000 naira has been written down by 240000 naira. It is now sold for 520000 naira. What is the gain on the sale?
items.s: Gain = proceeds - amount carried = 520000 - (720000 - 240000) = 40000 naira.

items.q: Rent paid during the year was 300000 naira. Rent owing at the start of the year was 30000 naira and rent owing at the end was 55000 naira. What is the charge for the year?
items.s: Charge = amount paid + closing amount owing - opening amount owing = 300000 + 55000 - 30000 = 325000 naira.

items.q: Insurance paid during the year was 210000 naira. Insurance paid in advance at the start of the year was 27000 naira and at the end it was 54000 naira. What is the charge for the year?
items.s: Charge = amount paid + opening amount in advance - closing amount in advance = 210000 + 27000 - 54000 = 183000 naira.

items.q: Interest received during the year was 210000 naira. Interest due at the start of the year was 32000 naira and interest due at the end was 58000 naira. What is the income for the year?
items.s: Income = amount received - opening amount due + closing amount due = 210000 - 32000 + 58000 = 236000 naira.

items.q: Trade receivables at the year end are 480000 naira. A provision of 5 percent is to be made against them. What is the amount of the provision?
items.s: Provision = receivables x rate/100 = 480000 x 5/100 = 24000 naira.

items.q: The provision against doubtful debts stood at 22000 naira at the start of the year and is to be 66000 naira at the end. What amount is charged against profit for the year?
items.s: Charge = closing provision - opening provision = 66000 - 22000 = 44000 naira.

items.q: A store held 200 units that cost 10 naira each and then bought 300 units at 24 naira each. 350 units were issued. Using FIFO, what is the cost of the units issued?
items.s: Under FIFO the issue is priced from the oldest units: 200 x 10 + 150 x 24 = 5600 naira.

items.q: A store held 300 units costing 20 naira each and bought 200 units costing 24 naira each. What is the weighted average cost per unit?
items.s: Weighted average = total cost/total units = (300 x 20 + 200 x 24)/(300 + 200) = 21.6 naira.

items.q: Goods that cost 180000 naira can be sold for 200000 naira after spending 50000 naira to finish them and 18000 naira to sell them. At what amount should they be carried?
items.s: Net realisable value = 200000 - 50000 - 18000 = 132000; stock is carried at the lower of 180000 and 132000, which is 132000 naira.

items.q: Purchases for the year were 320000 naira, carriage inwards was 18000 naira and returns outwards were 31000 naira. What figure is shown for net purchases?
items.s: Net purchases = purchases + carriage inwards - returns outwards = 320000 + 18000 - 31000 = 307000 naira.
items.t: Final accounts of a sole trader

items.q: Gross profit was 180000 naira, other income was 16000 naira and the expenses of the period were 162000 naira. What is the net profit?
items.s: Net profit = gross profit + other income - expenses = 180000 + 16000 - 162000 = 34000 naira.
items.t: Final accounts of a sole trader

items.q: A trader earns a gross profit of 25 percent on selling price. What is the mark-up on cost?
items.s: Mark-up = margin/(100 - margin) x 100 = 25/(100 - 25) x 100 = 33.33 percent.
items.t: Final accounts of a sole trader

items.q: Capital at the start of the year was 700000 naira, profit for the year was 210000 naira and capital at the end was 780000 naira. What were the drawings?
items.s: Drawings = opening capital + profit - closing capital = 700000 + 210000 - 780000 = 130000 naira.
items.t: Final accounts of a sole trader

items.q: A bank statement shows a credit balance of 615000 naira. Deposits of 38000 naira have not been credited and cheques of 47000 naira have not been presented. What is the corrected cash book balance?
items.s: Corrected balance = statement balance + uncredited deposits - unpresented cheques = 615000 + 38000 - 47000 = 606000 naira.

items.q: The receivables control account opens with a debit balance of 95000 naira. Credit sales were 495000 naira, receipts from customers were 340000 naira and returns inwards were 12000 naira. What is the closing balance?
items.s: Closing balance = opening balance + credit sales - receipts - returns = 95000 + 495000 - 340000 - 12000 = 238000 naira.

items.q: The payables control account opens with a credit balance of 148000 naira. Credit purchases were 425000 naira, payments to suppliers were 350000 naira and returns outwards were 15000 naira. What is the closing balance?
items.s: Closing balance = opening balance + credit purchases - payments - returns = 148000 + 425000 - 350000 - 15000 = 208000 naira.

items.q: A firm has total assets of 180000 naira and total liabilities of 135000 naira. What is the capital of the owner?
items.s: Capital = assets - liabilities = 180000 - 135000 = 45000 naira.

items.q: Which term is described by “the listing in which credit transactions with customers are entered before they reach the ledger”?
o: invoice
petty cash voucher
sales day book
credit note
items.s: sales day book is the listing in which credit transactions with customers are entered before they reach the ledger.

items.q: The statement “the posting of an amount to the correct class of account but to the wrong person” describes which of the following?
o: error of original entry
suspense account
error of principle
error of commission
items.s: error of commission is the posting of an amount to the correct class of account but to the wrong person.

items.q: The statement “a reduction obtained from a supplier for paying promptly” describes which of the following?
o: bad debt
discount allowed
bad debt recovered
discount received
items.s: discount received is a reduction obtained from a supplier for paying promptly.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines lower of cost and net realisable value.
o: the posting of an amount to the correct class of account but to the wrong person
the rule that stock is carried at whichever of the two amounts is smaller
the recording of both halves of a transaction on the wrong sides of their accounts
an amount incurred in the period but not paid by the end of it
items.s: lower of cost and net realisable value: the rule that stock is carried at whichever of the two amounts is smaller. The other options describe accrued expense, error of commission, complete reversal.

items.q: Which of the following best describes going concern?
o: the difference between the sales value of goods and what those goods cost the trader
the statement that shows the net result after all other income and expenses
the physical checking of the goods on hand at the year end
the assumption that the firm will remain in operation for the foreseeable future
items.s: going concern: the assumption that the firm will remain in operation for the foreseeable future. The other options describe inventory count, profit and loss account, gross profit.

items.q: Which term is described by “a schedule that explains why the figure for cash held by the firm differs from the figure sent by its bankers”?
o: bank reconciliation statement
standing order
unpresented cheque
bank charges
items.s: bank reconciliation statement is a schedule that explains why the figure for cash held by the firm differs from the figure sent by its bankers.

items.q: error of original entry may be defined as
o: the writing of a wrong figure in the books, which is then posted correctly to both sides
the amount at which an asset is carried after the charges made against it to date
the amount the firm expects to obtain for an asset at the very end of its use
the listing in which credit transactions with customers are entered before they reach the ledger
items.s: error of original entry: the writing of a wrong figure in the books, which is then posted correctly to both sides. The other options describe residual value, net book value, sales day book.

items.q: The statement “the physical checking of the goods on hand at the year end” describes which of the following?
o: fifo
inventory count
weighted average
lower of cost and net realisable value
items.s: inventory count is the physical checking of the goods on hand at the year end.

items.q: The statement “the costing method that assumes the oldest items on hand are the ones sold first” describes which of the following?
o: consignment stock
lower of cost and net realisable value
weighted average
fifo
items.s: fifo is the costing method that assumes the oldest items on hand are the ones sold first.

items.q: Which of the following best describes depreciation?
o: an account that totals the transactions with all credit customers
the costing method that assumes the oldest items on hand are the ones sold first
money collected before the service to which it relates has been given
the systematic allocation of the depreciable amount of an asset over the years it serves
items.s: depreciation: the systematic allocation of the depreciable amount of an asset over the years it serves. The other options describe fifo, income received in advance, sales ledger control.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines compensating error?
o: a reduction obtained from a supplier for paying promptly
two mistakes of equal amount on opposite sides that cancel each other out
the document sent by a seller showing the goods supplied and the amount payable by the buyer
the rule that every transaction is recorded twice, on opposite sides of two accounts
items.s: compensating error: two mistakes of equal amount on opposite sides that cancel each other out. The other options describe double entry, invoice, discount received.

items.q: Which of the following best describes provision for doubtful debts?
o: a charge raised against the possibility that some customers will never pay
the process of inserting the figure that makes the two sides of an account agree
the cancellation of an amount owed in both directions between the same two parties
money received from a customer whose account had earlier been written off
items.s: provision for doubtful debts: a charge raised against the possibility that some customers will never pay. The other options describe contra set off, balancing off, bad debt recovered.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines sales ledger control?
o: a schedule of what each customer owes, grouped by how long the amount has stood
the posting of an amount to the correct class of account but to the wrong person
an account that totals the transactions with all credit customers
the transfer of amounts from the day books to the accounts affected
items.s: sales ledger control: an account that totals the transactions with all credit customers. The other options describe error of commission, aged list of balances, posting.

items.q: Which term is described by “the method that charges a fixed percentage of the amount still carried in the books”?
o: net book value
disposal account
residual value
reducing balance
items.s: reducing balance is the method that charges a fixed percentage of the amount still carried in the books.

items.q: Which term is described by “the amount the firm expects to obtain for an asset at the very end of its use”?
o: provision for depreciation
reducing balance
residual value
net book value
items.s: residual value is the amount the firm expects to obtain for an asset at the very end of its use.

items.q: All of the following belong to Bank reconciliation EXCEPT
o: unpresented cheque
bank reconciliation statement
uncredited deposit
debit
items.s: Every other option belongs to Bank reconciliation. “debit” belongs to Ledger accounts and double entry, not Bank reconciliation.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines debit?
o: a reduction from the list price granted to a particular class of buyer
the left hand side of an account, used to record increases in assets and in expenses
the book used for transactions that fit none of the specialised day books
the rule that every transaction is recorded twice, on opposite sides of two accounts
items.s: debit: the left hand side of an account, used to record increases in assets and in expenses. The other options describe double entry, trade discount, journal proper.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines double entry.
o: a reduction given to a customer for paying promptly
amounts deducted by the firm's bankers for their services, known only from the record they send
the rule that every transaction is recorded twice, on opposite sides of two accounts
the document sent to a customer to reduce the amount owed after goods are returned
items.s: double entry: the rule that every transaction is recorded twice, on opposite sides of two accounts. The other options describe bank charges, discount allowed, credit note.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines discount received.
o: an amount paid in the period that belongs to a later period
a reduction obtained from a supplier for paying promptly
the document issued by a seller as evidence that money has been received
the rule that every transaction is recorded twice, on opposite sides of two accounts
items.s: discount received: a reduction obtained from a supplier for paying promptly. The other options describe receipt, double entry, prepayment.

items.q: Which term is described by “the document sent by a seller showing the goods supplied and the amount payable by the buyer”?
o: petty cash voucher
credit note
journal proper
invoice
items.s: invoice is the document sent by a seller showing the goods supplied and the amount payable by the buyer.
items.t: Source documents and books of original entry

items.q: All of the following belong to Accruals and prepayments EXCEPT
o: prepayment
contra set off
accrued income
accrued expense
items.s: Every other option belongs to Accruals and prepayments. “contra set off” belongs to Control accounts, not Accruals and prepayments.

items.q: The statement “recording income and expenses in the period they are earned or incurred rather than when money moves” describes which of the following?
o: business entity
consistency
accrual basis
historical cost
items.s: accrual basis is recording income and expenses in the period they are earned or incurred rather than when money moves.

items.q: The statement “an account that totals the transactions with all credit suppliers” describes which of the following?
o: contra set off
control account
purchases ledger control
sales ledger control
items.s: purchases ledger control is an account that totals the transactions with all credit suppliers.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines provision for doubtful debts.
o: the ledger record used to work out the gain or loss when an asset leaves the firm
an account that totals the transactions with all credit suppliers
a charge raised against the possibility that some customers will never pay
an instruction to the bank to pay a fixed amount at regular intervals
items.s: provision for doubtful debts: a charge raised against the possibility that some customers will never pay. The other options describe standing order, disposal account, purchases ledger control.

items.q: Which of the following best describes discount received?
o: the amount at which an asset is carried after the charges made against it to date
the left hand side of an account, used to record increases in assets and in expenses
a reduction obtained from a supplier for paying promptly
the recording of a capital item as revenue spending, or the reverse
items.s: discount received: a reduction obtained from a supplier for paying promptly. The other options describe error of principle, net book value, debit.

items.q: Which of the following best describes trade discount?
o: the listing of goods sent back to suppliers before they reach the ledger
the amount the firm expects to obtain for an asset at the very end of its use
the convention that treats the owner and the firm as two separate parties for record keeping
a reduction from the list price granted to a particular class of buyer
items.s: trade discount: a reduction from the list price granted to a particular class of buyer. The other options describe purchases returns book, business entity, residual value.

items.q: Which of the following best describes error of principle?
o: the recording of a capital item as revenue spending, or the reverse
the stake of the owner in the firm, being assets less outside obligations
the physical checking of the goods on hand at the year end
the difference between the sales value of goods and what those goods cost the trader
items.s: error of principle: the recording of a capital item as revenue spending, or the reverse. The other options describe gross profit, capital, inventory count.

items.q: control account may be defined as
o: the total amount set aside out of profit since an asset was bought
the document issued by a seller as evidence that money has been received
the statement that shows the gross result of buying and selling goods
a summary record whose balance should equal the total of the individual records it summarises
items.s: control account: a summary record whose balance should equal the total of the individual records it summarises. The other options describe receipt, trading account, provision for depreciation.

items.q: Which of the following best describes profit and loss account?
o: the method that charges an equal amount in each year of the life of the asset
a reduction from the list price granted to a particular class of buyer
the writing of a wrong figure in the books, which is then posted correctly to both sides
the statement that shows the net result after all other income and expenses
items.s: profit and loss account: the statement that shows the net result after all other income and expenses. The other options describe straight line, trade discount, error of original entry.
items.t: Final accounts of a sole trader

items.q: Which statement correctly defines purchases returns book?
o: the stake of the owner in the firm, being assets less outside obligations
the listing of goods sent back to suppliers before they reach the ledger
the rule that revenue is recognised only when a sale is complete and the buyer is committed
the rule that stock is carried at whichever of the two amounts is smaller
items.s: purchases returns book: the listing of goods sent back to suppliers before they reach the ledger. The other options describe lower of cost and net realisable value, realisation, capital.
items.t: Source documents and books of original entry

items.q: standing order may be defined as
o: the document sent to a customer to reduce the amount owed after goods are returned
an instruction to the bank to pay a fixed amount at regular intervals
the difference between the sales value of goods and what those goods cost the trader
money earned in the period but not yet received by the end of it
items.s: standing order: an instruction to the bank to pay a fixed amount at regular intervals. The other options describe credit note, gross profit, accrued income.

items.q: Which of the following best describes drawings?
o: money or goods taken out of the firm by its owner for private use
amounts deducted by the firm's bankers for their services, known only from the record they send
a temporary place that holds a difference until the cause is traced
a summary record whose balance should equal the total of the individual records it summarises
items.s: drawings: money or goods taken out of the firm by its owner for private use. The other options describe bank charges, suspense account, control account.
items.t: Final accounts of a sole trader

items.q: Which term is described by “money received from a customer whose account had earlier been written off”?
o: provision for doubtful debts
trade discount
discount allowed
bad debt recovered
items.s: bad debt recovered is money received from a customer whose account had earlier been written off.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines bank charges.
o: the excess of current resources over obligations falling due within a year
amounts deducted by the firm's bankers for their services, known only from the record they send
the document sent to a customer to reduce the amount owed after goods are returned
the estimated selling price less the costs still to be incurred and the costs of selling
items.s: bank charges: amounts deducted by the firm's bankers for their services, known only from the record they send. The other options describe credit note, working capital, net realisable value.

items.q: The statement “an amount incurred in the period but not paid by the end of it” describes which of the following?
o: income received in advance
accrued income
accrued expense
prepayment
items.s: accrued expense is an amount incurred in the period but not paid by the end of it.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines discount allowed?
o: the document sent to a customer to correct an undercharge on a previous bill
recording income and expenses in the period they are earned or incurred rather than when money moves
a reduction given to a customer for paying promptly
an instruction to the bank to pay a fixed amount at regular intervals
items.s: discount allowed: a reduction given to a customer for paying promptly. The other options describe standing order, accrual basis, debit note.

items.q: The statement “the rule that expenses are set against the revenue of the period they helped to earn” describes which of the following?
o: matching
accrued income
income received in advance
accrued expense
items.s: matching is the rule that expenses are set against the revenue of the period they helped to earn.

items.q: discount received may be defined as
o: goods held by a trader but still owned by the supplier until sold
the rule that only items big enough to influence the judgement of a user need separate disclosure
a reduction obtained from a supplier for paying promptly
the total amount set aside out of profit since an asset was bought
items.s: discount received: a reduction obtained from a supplier for paying promptly. The other options describe materiality, consignment stock, provision for depreciation.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines debit note?
o: a list of ledger balances taken out to check that total left side amounts equal total right side amounts
the document sent to a customer to correct an undercharge on a previous bill
an amount incurred in the period but not paid by the end of it
a schedule of what each customer owes, grouped by how long the amount has stood
items.s: debit note: the document sent to a customer to correct an undercharge on a previous bill. The other options describe accrued expense, trial balance, aged list of balances.
items.t: Source documents and books of original entry

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines accrued income.
o: the stake of the owner in the firm, being assets less outside obligations
the excess of current resources over obligations falling due within a year
money earned in the period but not yet received by the end of it
the cancellation of an amount owed in both directions between the same two parties
items.s: accrued income: money earned in the period but not yet received by the end of it. The other options describe contra set off, capital, working capital.

items.q: contra set off may be defined as
o: the document sent to a customer to reduce the amount owed after goods are returned
the cancellation of an amount owed in both directions between the same two parties
the convention of carrying assets at the amount paid to acquire them
the listing of goods sent back to suppliers before they reach the ledger
items.s: contra set off: the cancellation of an amount owed in both directions between the same two parties. The other options describe historical cost, credit note, purchases returns book.

items.q: The statement “the listing of goods sent back to suppliers before they reach the ledger” describes which of the following?
o: petty cash voucher
sales day book
purchases returns book
debit note
items.s: purchases returns book is the listing of goods sent back to suppliers before they reach the ledger.
items.t: Source documents and books of original entry

items.q: The statement “the stake of the owner in the firm, being assets less outside obligations” describes which of the following?
o: gross profit
capital
working capital
trading account
items.s: capital is the stake of the owner in the firm, being assets less outside obligations.
items.t: Final accounts of a sole trader

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines net book value.
o: the amount at which an asset is carried after the charges made against it to date
the assumption that the firm will remain in operation for the foreseeable future
the document sent to a customer to reduce the amount owed after goods are returned
the right hand side of an account, used to record increases in liabilities, capital and income
items.s: net book value: the amount at which an asset is carried after the charges made against it to date. The other options describe going concern, credit note, credit.

items.q: purchases ledger control may be defined as
o: an account that totals the transactions with all credit customers
the cancellation of an amount owed in both directions between the same two parties
an account that totals the transactions with all credit suppliers
the rule that revenue is recognised only when a sale is complete and the buyer is committed
items.s: purchases ledger control: an account that totals the transactions with all credit suppliers. The other options describe sales ledger control, contra set off, realisation.

items.q: The statement “the convention of recognising losses as soon as they are foreseen but gains only when they are certain” describes which of the following?
o: business entity
going concern
accrual basis
prudence
items.s: prudence is the convention of recognising losses as soon as they are foreseen but gains only when they are certain.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines unpresented cheque?
o: money paid in by the firm that the bank has not yet added to the account
a summary record whose balance should equal the total of the individual records it summarises
the ledger record used to work out the gain or loss when an asset leaves the firm
a payment instrument issued by the firm that its bankers have not yet debited
items.s: unpresented cheque: a payment instrument issued by the firm that its bankers have not yet debited. The other options describe uncredited deposit, disposal account, control account.

items.q: The statement “the rule that every transaction is recorded twice, on opposite sides of two accounts” describes which of the following?
o: posting
debit
double entry
balancing off
items.s: double entry is the rule that every transaction is recorded twice, on opposite sides of two accounts.

items.q: Which of the following best describes income received in advance?
o: the listing of goods sent back to suppliers before they reach the ledger
money collected before the service to which it relates has been given
the failure to record a transaction at all, so that the trial balance still agrees
money earned in the period but not yet received by the end of it
items.s: income received in advance: money collected before the service to which it relates has been given. The other options describe error of omission, accrued income, purchases returns book.

items.q: Which term is described by “the right hand side of an account, used to record increases in liabilities, capital and income”?
o: debit
posting
balancing off
credit
items.s: credit is the right hand side of an account, used to record increases in liabilities, capital and income.

items.q: The statement “goods held by a trader but still owned by the supplier until sold” describes which of the following?
o: fifo
net realisable value
weighted average
consignment stock
items.s: consignment stock is goods held by a trader but still owned by the supplier until sold.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines consistency?
o: the excess of current resources over obligations falling due within a year
the transfer of amounts from the day books to the accounts affected
the convention of applying the same accounting methods from one period to the next
recording income and expenses in the period they are earned or incurred rather than when money moves
items.s: consistency: the convention of applying the same accounting methods from one period to the next. The other options describe accrual basis, working capital, posting.

items.q: Which of the following best describes inventory count?
o: the physical checking of the goods on hand at the year end
the convention of recognising losses as soon as they are foreseen but gains only when they are certain
the book used for transactions that fit none of the specialised day books
the listing in which credit transactions with customers are entered before they reach the ledger
items.s: inventory count: the physical checking of the goods on hand at the year end. The other options describe prudence, journal proper, sales day book.

items.q: Which term is described by “a schedule of what each customer owes, grouped by how long the amount has stood”?
o: aged list of balances
sales ledger control
contra set off
control account
items.s: aged list of balances is a schedule of what each customer owes, grouped by how long the amount has stood.

items.q: Which term is described by “the systematic allocation of the depreciable amount of an asset over the years it serves”?
o: straight line
provision for depreciation
depreciation
disposal account
items.s: depreciation is the systematic allocation of the depreciable amount of an asset over the years it serves.

items.q: Which of the following best describes credit?
o: a summary record whose balance should equal the total of the individual records it summarises
the rule that revenue is recognised only when a sale is complete and the buyer is committed
the right hand side of an account, used to record increases in liabilities, capital and income
the physical checking of the goods on hand at the year end
items.s: credit: the right hand side of an account, used to record increases in liabilities, capital and income. The other options describe control account, inventory count, realisation.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines aged list of balances?
o: the statement that shows the gross result of buying and selling goods
a schedule of what each customer owes, grouped by how long the amount has stood
the method that charges a fixed percentage of the amount still carried in the books
the physical checking of the goods on hand at the year end
items.s: aged list of balances: a schedule of what each customer owes, grouped by how long the amount has stood. The other options describe inventory count, trading account, reducing balance.

items.q: The statement “the right hand side of an account, used to record increases in liabilities, capital and income” describes which of the following?
o: credit
balancing off
ledger
posting
items.s: credit is the right hand side of an account, used to record increases in liabilities, capital and income.

items.q: fifo may be defined as
o: the costing method that assumes the oldest items on hand are the ones sold first
the excess of current resources over obligations falling due within a year
the method that charges a fixed percentage of the amount still carried in the books
a schedule of what each customer owes, grouped by how long the amount has stood
items.s: fifo: the costing method that assumes the oldest items on hand are the ones sold first. The other options describe working capital, reducing balance, aged list of balances.

items.q: Which of the following best describes bank reconciliation statement?
o: the convention of applying the same accounting methods from one period to the next
the method that charges a fixed percentage of the amount still carried in the books
a schedule that explains why the figure for cash held by the firm differs from the figure sent by its bankers
money or goods taken out of the firm by its owner for private use
items.s: bank reconciliation statement: a schedule that explains why the figure for cash held by the firm differs from the figure sent by its bankers. The other options describe consistency, drawings, reducing balance.

items.q: Which term is described by “the left hand side of an account, used to record increases in assets and in expenses”?
o: ledger
balancing off
debit
credit
items.s: debit is the left hand side of an account, used to record increases in assets and in expenses.

items.q: Which of the following best describes error of original entry?
o: the writing of a wrong figure in the books, which is then posted correctly to both sides
the systematic allocation of the depreciable amount of an asset over the years it serves
the listing in which credit transactions with customers are entered before they reach the ledger
money or goods taken out of the firm by its owner for private use
items.s: error of original entry: the writing of a wrong figure in the books, which is then posted correctly to both sides. The other options describe depreciation, sales day book, drawings.

items.q: Which term is described by “the slip that supports every small payment made out of the office float”?
o: sales day book
credit note
debit note
petty cash voucher
items.s: petty cash voucher is the slip that supports every small payment made out of the office float.
items.t: Source documents and books of original entry

items.q: Which term is described by “the listing of goods sent back to suppliers before they reach the ledger”?
o: receipt
invoice
purchases returns book
petty cash voucher
items.s: purchases returns book is the listing of goods sent back to suppliers before they reach the ledger.
items.t: Source documents and books of original entry

items.q: Which term is described by “the recording of a capital item as revenue spending, or the reverse”?
o: error of principle
suspense account
error of omission
complete reversal
items.s: error of principle is the recording of a capital item as revenue spending, or the reverse.

items.q: Equipment costing 600000 naira is expected to be worth 30000 naira after 5 years and is written off evenly. What is the total charged against profit after 2 years?
items.s: Total charge = years x (cost - end value)/life = 2 x (600000 - 30000)/5 = 228000 naira.

items.q: An asset is bought for 600000 naira and is written down at 20 percent each year on the reducing balance. What is the charge for the first year?
items.s: First year charge = cost x rate = 600000 x 20/100 = 120000 naira.

items.q: Rent paid during the year was 180000 naira. Rent owing at the start of the year was 30000 naira and rent owing at the end was 45000 naira. What is the charge for the year?
items.s: Charge = amount paid + closing amount owing - opening amount owing = 180000 + 45000 - 30000 = 195000 naira.

items.q: Trade receivables at the year end are 240000 naira. A provision of 2 percent is to be made against them. What is the amount of the provision?
items.s: Provision = receivables x rate/100 = 240000 x 2/100 = 4800 naira.

items.q: Purchases for the year were 320000 naira, carriage inwards was 34000 naira and returns outwards were 43000 naira. What figure is shown for net purchases?
items.s: Net purchases = purchases + carriage inwards - returns outwards = 320000 + 34000 - 43000 = 311000 naira.
items.t: Final accounts of a sole trader

items.q: Gross profit was 320000 naira, other income was 28000 naira and the expenses of the period were 95000 naira. What is the net profit?
items.s: Net profit = gross profit + other income - expenses = 320000 + 28000 - 95000 = 253000 naira.
items.t: Final accounts of a sole trader

items.q: A firm has total assets of 625000 naira and total liabilities of 96000 naira. What is the capital of the owner?
items.s: Capital = assets - liabilities = 625000 - 96000 = 529000 naira.

items.q: A machine costing 360000 naira has an expected value of 100000 naira at the end of its life of 4 years. What is the yearly charge using the straight line method?
items.s: Yearly charge = (cost - end value)/life = (360000 - 100000)/4 = 65000 naira.

items.q: A vehicle costing 300000 naira has a scrap value of 60000 naira and a life of 5 years and is written off evenly. What amount is carried in the books after 3 years?
items.s: Amount carried = cost - years x (cost - scrap)/life = 300000 - 3 x (300000 - 60000)/5 = 156000 naira.

items.q: A plant costing 400000 naira is written down at 25 percent each year on the reducing balance. What amount is carried in the books at the end of 4 years?
items.s: Amount carried = cost x (1 - rate/100)^years = 400000 x (1 - 25/100)^4 = 126562.5 naira.

items.q: Insurance paid during the year was 210000 naira. Insurance paid in advance at the start of the year was 36000 naira and at the end it was 42000 naira. What is the charge for the year?
items.s: Charge = amount paid + opening amount in advance - closing amount in advance = 210000 + 36000 - 42000 = 204000 naira.

items.q: Interest received during the year was 140000 naira. Interest due at the start of the year was 32000 naira and interest due at the end was 58000 naira. What is the income for the year?
items.s: Income = amount received - opening amount due + closing amount due = 140000 - 32000 + 58000 = 166000 naira.

items.q: A trader has receivables of 465000 naira. A customer who owes 25000 naira is declared unable to pay and the amount is written off. What figure for receivables remains?
items.s: Remaining receivables = 465000 - 25000 = 440000 naira.

items.q: The provision against doubtful debts stood at 22000 naira at the start of the year and is to be 40000 naira at the end. What amount is charged against profit for the year?
items.s: Charge = closing provision - opening provision = 40000 - 22000 = 18000 naira.

items.q: Goods with a list price of 480000 naira are sold subject to a trade discount of 20 percent. What is the amount charged to the customer?
items.s: Amount charged = list price x (100 - discount)/100 = 480000 x (100 - 20)/100 = 384000 naira.

items.q: A store held 300 units that cost 15 naira each and then bought 200 units at 18 naira each. 400 units were issued. Using FIFO, what is the cost of the units issued?
items.s: Under FIFO the issue is priced from the oldest units: 300 x 15 + 100 x 18 = 6300 naira.

items.q: A store held 200 units costing 20 naira each and bought 300 units costing 30 naira each. What is the weighted average cost per unit?
items.s: Weighted average = total cost/total units = (200 x 20 + 300 x 30)/(200 + 300) = 26 naira.

items.q: Goods that cost 250000 naira can be sold for 290000 naira after spending 20000 naira to finish them and 26000 naira to sell them. At what amount should they be carried?
items.s: Net realisable value = 290000 - 20000 - 26000 = 244000; stock is carried at the lower of 250000 and 244000, which is 244000 naira.

items.q: Opening stock was 60000 naira, purchases were 240000 naira and closing stock was 78000 naira. What is the cost of the goods sold?
items.s: Cost of goods sold = opening stock + purchases - closing stock = 60000 + 240000 - 78000 = 222000 naira.
items.t: Final accounts of a sole trader

items.q: Sales for the year were 940000 naira and the cost of the goods sold was 410000 naira. What is the gross profit?
items.s: Gross profit = sales - cost of goods sold = 940000 - 410000 = 530000 naira.
items.t: Final accounts of a sole trader

items.q: Goods costing 120000 naira are to be sold at a mark-up of 40 percent on cost. What is the selling price?
items.s: Selling price = cost x (100 + mark-up)/100 = 120000 x (100 + 40)/100 = 168000 naira.
items.t: Final accounts of a sole trader

items.q: A trader earns a gross profit of 40 percent on selling price. What is the mark-up on cost?
items.s: Mark-up = margin/(100 - margin) x 100 = 40/(100 - 40) x 100 = 66.67 percent.
items.t: Final accounts of a sole trader

items.q: The receivables control account opens with a debit balance of 130000 naira. Credit sales were 560000 naira, receipts from customers were 210000 naira and returns inwards were 12000 naira. What is the closing balance?
items.s: Closing balance = opening balance + credit sales - receipts - returns = 130000 + 560000 - 210000 - 12000 = 468000 naira.

items.q: The payables control account opens with a credit balance of 105000 naira. Credit purchases were 530000 naira, payments to suppliers were 440000 naira and returns outwards were 23000 naira. What is the closing balance?
items.s: Closing balance = opening balance + credit purchases - payments - returns = 105000 + 530000 - 440000 - 23000 = 172000 naira.

items.q: A petty cash float of 20000 naira is reimbursed at the end of the month when 4650 naira is left in the box. How much is paid back into the float?
items.s: Reimbursement = float - cash left = 20000 - 4650 = 15350 naira.
items.t: Source documents and books of original entry

items.q: The debit column of a trial balance totals 580000 naira and the credit column totals 559000 naira. What amount is carried to the suspense account?
items.s: Suspense = difference between the two columns = 580000 - 559000 = 21000 naira.

items.t: Final accounts of a sole trader

items.q: A bank statement shows a credit balance of 615000 naira. Deposits of 38000 naira have not been credited and cheques of 31000 naira have not been presented. What is the corrected cash book balance?
items.s: Corrected balance = statement balance + uncredited deposits - unpresented cheques = 615000 + 38000 - 31000 = 622000 naira.

items.q: A machine costing 360000 naira has an expected value of 60000 naira at the end of its life of 10 years. What is the yearly charge using the straight line method?
items.s: Yearly charge = (cost - end value)/life = (360000 - 60000)/10 = 30000 naira.

items.q: A plant costing 500000 naira is written down at 10 percent each year on the reducing balance. What amount is carried in the books at the end of 2 years?
items.s: Amount carried = cost x (1 - rate/100)^years = 500000 x (1 - 10/100)^2 = 405000 naira.

items.q: Insurance paid during the year was 150000 naira. Insurance paid in advance at the start of the year was 18000 naira and at the end it was 42000 naira. What is the charge for the year?
items.s: Charge = amount paid + opening amount in advance - closing amount in advance = 150000 + 18000 - 42000 = 126000 naira.

items.q: Interest received during the year was 90000 naira. Interest due at the start of the year was 32000 naira and interest due at the end was 74000 naira. What is the income for the year?
items.s: Income = amount received - opening amount due + closing amount due = 90000 - 32000 + 74000 = 132000 naira.

items.q: A trader has receivables of 380000 naira. A customer who owes 38000 naira is declared unable to pay and the amount is written off. What figure for receivables remains?
items.s: Remaining receivables = 380000 - 38000 = 342000 naira.

items.q: The provision against doubtful debts stood at 15000 naira at the start of the year and is to be 40000 naira at the end. What amount is charged against profit for the year?
items.s: Charge = closing provision - opening provision = 40000 - 15000 = 25000 naira.

items.q: Goods with a list price of 200000 naira are sold subject to a trade discount of 10 percent. What is the amount charged to the customer?
items.s: Amount charged = list price x (100 - discount)/100 = 200000 x (100 - 10)/100 = 180000 naira.

items.s: Under FIFO the issue is priced from the oldest units: 200 x 12 + 100 x 24 = 4800 naira.

items.s: Weighted average = total cost/total units = (300 x 12 + 300 x 26)/(300 + 300) = 19 naira.

items.q: Goods that cost 250000 naira can be sold for 290000 naira after spending 35000 naira to finish them and 10000 naira to sell them. At what amount should they be carried?

items.q: A trader adds 33 percent to the cost of goods when fixing the price. What is the gross profit as a percentage of the selling price?
items.s: Margin = mark-up/(100 + mark-up) x 100 = 33/(100 + 33) x 100 = 24.81 percent.
items.t: Final accounts of a sole trader

items.q: Capital at the start of the year was 700000 naira, profit for the year was 120000 naira and capital at the end was 780000 naira. What were the drawings?
items.s: Drawings = opening capital + profit - closing capital = 700000 + 120000 - 780000 = 40000 naira.
items.t: Final accounts of a sole trader

items.q: The provision against doubtful debts stood at 30000 naira at the start of the year and is to be 66000 naira at the end. What amount is charged against profit for the year?

items.q: A store held 400 units costing 12 naira each and bought 100 units costing 24 naira each. What is the weighted average cost per unit?

items.q: Goods that cost 180000 naira can be sold for 200000 naira after spending 20000 naira to finish them and 26000 naira to sell them. At what amount should they be carried?

items.q: A trader adds 15 percent to the cost of goods when fixing the price. What is the gross profit as a percentage of the selling price?

items.q: An asset is bought for 200000 naira and is written down at 10 percent each year on the reducing balance. What is the charge for the first year?
items.s: First year charge = cost x rate = 200000 x 10/100 = 20000 naira.

items.q: A plant costing 250000 naira is written down at 20 percent each year on the reducing balance. What amount is carried in the books at the end of 4 years?

items.q: Rent paid during the year was 120000 naira. Rent owing at the start of the year was 10000 naira and rent owing at the end was 55000 naira. What is the charge for the year?

items.q: Interest received during the year was 140000 naira. Interest due at the start of the year was 12000 naira and interest due at the end was 45000 naira. What is the income for the year?

items.q: A store held 300 units that cost 12 naira each and then bought 300 units at 18 naira each. 400 units were issued. Using FIFO, what is the cost of the units issued?

items.q: Opening stock was 95000 naira, purchases were 240000 naira and closing stock was 55000 naira. What is the cost of the goods sold?

items.q: Purchases for the year were 455000 naira, carriage inwards was 34000 naira and returns outwards were 22000 naira. What figure is shown for net purchases?

items.t: Final accounts of a sole trader

items.q: Gross profit was 245000 naira, other income was 16000 naira and the expenses of the period were 128000 naira. What is the net profit?

items.t: Final accounts of a sole trader

items.q: The payables control account opens with a credit balance of 105000 naira. Credit purchases were 310000 naira, payments to suppliers were 260000 naira and returns outwards were 15000 naira. What is the closing balance?

items.q: A petty cash float of 30000 naira is reimbursed at the end of the month when 4650 naira is left in the box. How much is paid back into the float?

items.q: Insurance paid during the year was 150000 naira. Insurance paid in advance at the start of the year was 27000 naira and at the end it was 42000 naira. What is the charge for the year?

items.q: A store held 300 units costing 16 naira each and bought 100 units costing 30 naira each. What is the weighted average cost per unit?

items.q: An asset bought for 720000 naira has been written down by 180000 naira. It is now sold for 565000 naira. What is the gain on the sale?

items.q: Which of the following best describes trading account?
o: the stake of the owner in the firm, being assets less outside obligations
the statement that shows the gross result of buying and selling goods
money or goods taken out of the firm by its owner for private use
the excess of current resources over obligations falling due within a year
items.s: trading account: the statement that shows the gross result of buying and selling goods. The other options describe drawings, working capital, capital.
items.t: Final accounts of a sole trader

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “the recording of a capital item as revenue spending, or the reverse”
o: complete reversal
error of commission
error of omission
error of principle
items.s: error of principle is the recording of a capital item as revenue spending, or the reverse.

items.q: error of omission may be defined as
o: the recording of a capital item as revenue spending, or the reverse
the recording of both halves of a transaction on the wrong sides of their accounts
the failure to record a transaction at all, so that the trial balance still agrees
two mistakes of equal amount on opposite sides that cancel each other out
items.s: error of omission: the failure to record a transaction at all, so that the trial balance still agrees. The other options describe error of principle, complete reversal, compensating error.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “the writing of a wrong figure in the books, which is then posted correctly to both sides”
o: error of commission
suspense account
error of original entry
error of omission
items.s: error of original entry is the writing of a wrong figure in the books, which is then posted correctly to both sides.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “an amount owed by a customer that is judged irrecoverable and removed from the books”
o: provision for doubtful debts
trade discount
bad debt
bad debt recovered
items.s: bad debt is an amount owed by a customer that is judged irrecoverable and removed from the books.

items.q: Which of the following best describes materiality?
o: the convention of recognising losses as soon as they are foreseen but gains only when they are certain
the rule that only items big enough to influence the judgement of a user need separate disclosure
the convention that treats the owner and the firm as two separate parties for record keeping
recording income and expenses in the period they are earned or incurred rather than when money moves
items.s: materiality: the rule that only items big enough to influence the judgement of a user need separate disclosure. The other options describe business entity, accrual basis, prudence.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines error of original entry.
o: the recording of both halves of a transaction on the wrong sides of their accounts
the writing of a wrong figure in the books, which is then posted correctly to both sides
the posting of an amount to the correct class of account but to the wrong person
the recording of a capital item as revenue spending, or the reverse
items.s: error of original entry: the writing of a wrong figure in the books, which is then posted correctly to both sides. The other options describe complete reversal, error of principle, error of commission.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines suspense account.
o: the posting of an amount to the correct class of account but to the wrong person
the failure to record a transaction at all, so that the trial balance still agrees
a temporary place that holds a difference until the cause is traced
two mistakes of equal amount on opposite sides that cancel each other out
items.s: suspense account: a temporary place that holds a difference until the cause is traced. The other options describe error of omission, compensating error, error of commission.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “the systematic allocation of the depreciable amount of an asset over the years it serves”
o: depreciation
provision for depreciation
disposal account
net book value
items.s: depreciation is the systematic allocation of the depreciable amount of an asset over the years it serves.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “the document sent by a seller showing the goods supplied and the amount payable by the buyer”
o: debit note
invoice
journal proper
sales day book
items.s: invoice is the document sent by a seller showing the goods supplied and the amount payable by the buyer.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines prepayment.
o: an amount incurred in the period but not paid by the end of it
the rule that expenses are set against the revenue of the period they helped to earn
money earned in the period but not yet received by the end of it
an amount paid in the period that belongs to a later period
items.s: prepayment: an amount paid in the period that belongs to a later period. The other options describe matching, accrued expense, accrued income.

items.q: unpresented cheque is best described as
o: money paid in by the firm that the bank has not yet added to the account
an instruction to the bank to pay a fixed amount at regular intervals
a schedule that explains why the figure for cash held by the firm differs from the figure sent by its bankers
a payment instrument issued by the firm that its bankers have not yet debited
items.s: unpresented cheque: a payment instrument issued by the firm that its bankers have not yet debited. The other options describe bank reconciliation statement, standing order, uncredited deposit.

items.q: credit note is best described as
o: the book used for transactions that fit none of the specialised day books
the document issued by a seller as evidence that money has been received
the document sent to a customer to reduce the amount owed after goods are returned
the listing of goods sent back to suppliers before they reach the ledger
items.s: credit note: the document sent to a customer to reduce the amount owed after goods are returned. The other options describe journal proper, receipt, purchases returns book.
items.t: Source documents and books of original entry

items.q: error of principle is best described as
o: the posting of an amount to the correct class of account but to the wrong person
the recording of a capital item as revenue spending, or the reverse
two mistakes of equal amount on opposite sides that cancel each other out
a temporary place that holds a difference until the cause is traced
items.s: error of principle: the recording of a capital item as revenue spending, or the reverse. The other options describe error of commission, suspense account, compensating error.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines journal proper.
o: the document sent to a customer to reduce the amount owed after goods are returned
the book used for transactions that fit none of the specialised day books
the slip that supports every small payment made out of the office float
the listing in which credit transactions with customers are entered before they reach the ledger
items.s: journal proper: the book used for transactions that fit none of the specialised day books. The other options describe petty cash voucher, sales day book, credit note.
items.t: Source documents and books of original entry

items.q: posting may be defined as
o: the process of inserting the figure that makes the two sides of an account agree
the principal book of account in which transactions are classified under account headings
a list of ledger balances taken out to check that total left side amounts equal total right side amounts
the transfer of amounts from the day books to the accounts affected
items.s: posting: the transfer of amounts from the day books to the accounts affected. The other options describe trial balance, ledger, balancing off.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines accrued expense?
o: money earned in the period but not yet received by the end of it
an amount paid in the period that belongs to a later period
the rule that expenses are set against the revenue of the period they helped to earn
an amount incurred in the period but not paid by the end of it
items.s: accrued expense: an amount incurred in the period but not paid by the end of it. The other options describe accrued income, matching, prepayment.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “money or goods taken out of the firm by its owner for private use”
o: drawings
gross profit
profit and loss account
trading account
items.s: drawings is money or goods taken out of the firm by its owner for private use.
items.t: Final accounts of a sole trader

items.q: consignment stock may be defined as
o: goods held by a trader but still owned by the supplier until sold
the physical checking of the goods on hand at the year end
the costing method that assumes the oldest items on hand are the ones sold first
the rule that stock is carried at whichever of the two amounts is smaller
items.s: consignment stock: goods held by a trader but still owned by the supplier until sold. The other options describe inventory count, fifo, lower of cost and net realisable value.

items.q: income received in advance is best described as
o: money collected before the service to which it relates has been given
an amount incurred in the period but not paid by the end of it
the rule that expenses are set against the revenue of the period they helped to earn
an amount paid in the period that belongs to a later period
items.s: income received in advance: money collected before the service to which it relates has been given. The other options describe accrued expense, matching, prepayment.

items.q: Which of the following best describes straight line?
o: the amount the firm expects to obtain for an asset at the very end of its use
the ledger record used to work out the gain or loss when an asset leaves the firm
the total amount set aside out of profit since an asset was bought
the method that charges an equal amount in each year of the life of the asset
items.s: straight line: the method that charges an equal amount in each year of the life of the asset. The other options describe residual value, disposal account, provision for depreciation.

items.q: trade discount may be defined as
o: a charge raised against the possibility that some customers will never pay
a reduction from the list price granted to a particular class of buyer
a reduction given to a customer for paying promptly
a reduction obtained from a supplier for paying promptly
items.s: trade discount: a reduction from the list price granted to a particular class of buyer. The other options describe discount received, discount allowed, provision for doubtful debts.

items.q: purchases returns book is best described as
o: the book used for transactions that fit none of the specialised day books
the listing in which credit transactions with customers are entered before they reach the ledger
the listing of goods sent back to suppliers before they reach the ledger
the document sent to a customer to correct an undercharge on a previous bill
items.s: purchases returns book: the listing of goods sent back to suppliers before they reach the ledger. The other options describe journal proper, sales day book, debit note.
items.t: Source documents and books of original entry

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines reducing balance.
o: the total amount set aside out of profit since an asset was bought
the method that charges a fixed percentage of the amount still carried in the books
the systematic allocation of the depreciable amount of an asset over the years it serves
the method that charges an equal amount in each year of the life of the asset
items.s: reducing balance: the method that charges a fixed percentage of the amount still carried in the books. The other options describe provision for depreciation, depreciation, straight line.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines sales day book?
o: the listing in which credit transactions with customers are entered before they reach the ledger
the listing of goods sent back to suppliers before they reach the ledger
the document sent to a customer to reduce the amount owed after goods are returned
the document sent to a customer to correct an undercharge on a previous bill
items.s: sales day book: the listing in which credit transactions with customers are entered before they reach the ledger. The other options describe debit note, credit note, purchases returns book.
items.t: Source documents and books of original entry

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “a temporary place that holds a difference until the cause is traced”
o: compensating error
suspense account
error of original entry
error of commission
items.s: suspense account is a temporary place that holds a difference until the cause is traced.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines provision for depreciation?
o: the method that charges an equal amount in each year of the life of the asset
the method that charges a fixed percentage of the amount still carried in the books
the systematic allocation of the depreciable amount of an asset over the years it serves
the total amount set aside out of profit since an asset was bought
items.s: provision for depreciation: the total amount set aside out of profit since an asset was bought. The other options describe reducing balance, straight line, depreciation.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines invoice?
o: the document issued by a seller as evidence that money has been received
the document sent by a seller showing the goods supplied and the amount payable by the buyer
the slip that supports every small payment made out of the office float
the listing of goods sent back to suppliers before they reach the ledger
items.s: invoice: the document sent by a seller showing the goods supplied and the amount payable by the buyer. The other options describe purchases returns book, petty cash voucher, receipt.
items.t: Source documents and books of original entry

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “the right hand side of an account, used to record increases in liabilities, capital and income”
o: double entry
credit
balancing off
trial balance
items.s: credit is the right hand side of an account, used to record increases in liabilities, capital and income.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines disposal account?
o: the total amount set aside out of profit since an asset was bought
the ledger record used to work out the gain or loss when an asset leaves the firm
the method that charges a fixed percentage of the amount still carried in the books
the amount at which an asset is carried after the charges made against it to date
items.s: disposal account: the ledger record used to work out the gain or loss when an asset leaves the firm. The other options describe provision for depreciation, reducing balance, net book value.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines weighted average?
o: goods held by a trader but still owned by the supplier until sold
the costing method that assumes the oldest items on hand are the ones sold first
the estimated selling price less the costs still to be incurred and the costs of selling
the method that divides the total cost of goods available by the total quantity available
items.s: weighted average: the method that divides the total cost of goods available by the total quantity available. The other options describe consignment stock, fifo, net realisable value.

items.q: Which of the following best describes uncredited deposit?
o: money paid in by the firm that the bank has not yet added to the account
amounts deducted by the firm's bankers for their services, known only from the record they send
an instruction to the bank to pay a fixed amount at regular intervals
a schedule that explains why the figure for cash held by the firm differs from the figure sent by its bankers
items.s: uncredited deposit: money paid in by the firm that the bank has not yet added to the account. The other options describe bank reconciliation statement, standing order, bank charges.

items.q: Which of the following best describes prepayment?
o: money earned in the period but not yet received by the end of it
an amount paid in the period that belongs to a later period
an amount incurred in the period but not paid by the end of it
the rule that expenses are set against the revenue of the period they helped to earn
items.s: prepayment: an amount paid in the period that belongs to a later period. The other options describe accrued expense, accrued income, matching.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines straight line?
o: the amount the firm expects to obtain for an asset at the very end of its use
the method that charges an equal amount in each year of the life of the asset
the systematic allocation of the depreciable amount of an asset over the years it serves
the method that charges a fixed percentage of the amount still carried in the books
items.s: straight line: the method that charges an equal amount in each year of the life of the asset. The other options describe depreciation, reducing balance, residual value.

items.q: Which term is described by “the physical checking of the goods on hand at the year end”?
o: net realisable value
fifo
inventory count
weighted average
items.s: inventory count is the physical checking of the goods on hand at the year end.

items.q: Which term is described by “the statement that shows the gross result of buying and selling goods”?

trading account
working capital

items.q: An asset bought for 400000 naira has been written down by 240000 naira. It is now sold for 185000 naira. What is the gain on the sale?
items.s: Gain = proceeds - amount carried = 185000 - (400000 - 240000) = 25000 naira.

items.q: Rent paid during the year was 120000 naira. Rent owing at the start of the year was 20000 naira and rent owing at the end was 45000 naira. What is the charge for the year?
items.s: Charge = amount paid + closing amount owing - opening amount owing = 120000 + 45000 - 20000 = 145000 naira.
